headline: Highest risk is B data leakage: Prefect’s broad network egress can transmit Marker-derived content if the pair is wired into a shared workflow, while prompt injection and capability conflict are otherwise limited by Marker’s…

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Marker has no filesystem write, no network egress, and no MCP/browser surfaces, so it cannot directly bridge into Prefect by default. A prompt-injection pathway only appears if an operator manually copies Marker output into Prefect-managed content or a shared workspace is introduced. Prefect can then consume that content, but the bridge is unusual and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Marker output into a Prefect task or flow input, THEN injected instructions can propagate.
IF a shared workspace is added between the agents, THEN Marker-authored content can be treated as input by Prefect.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of raw model output into Prefect task definitions.
Add a review step before Prefect consumes Marker output.
Use a fixed schema for Marker outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between producer and consumer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Marker is documented as open-source document-processing with no network egress, while Prefect has broad network egress and API calls. If both are placed in a shared workspace or workflow, Marker-derived documents or metadata can flow into Prefect and then out over the network. The pairwise leakage path exists in default orchestration patterns, though not proven from a shared filesystem in the profiles.
conditions: IF Marker outputs are passed into Prefect tasks, THEN those contents can be transmitted by Prefect.
IF the two agents share a workspace or pipeline artifact store, THEN document contents or workflow metadata can leak outward.
mitigations: Restrict Prefect tasks to metadata-only inputs.
Separate sensitive documents from Prefect-accessible artifacts.
Turn off any unnecessary Prefect API integrations.
Add a manual approval step before networked tasks.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention checks on Prefect inputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Marker cannot write files, modify git, or use subprocesses, so it has little direct write overlap with Prefect. Prefect does have orchestration and API-calling capability, but the profiles do not show shared mutable resources or locking conflicts. Any conflict would require an added shared target such as a workspace or repo, making the pathway unusual and bounded.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external resource, THEN race conditions can occur.
IF Prefect is pointed at a shared mutable repo or workspace, THEN coordination issues become possible.
mitigations: Avoid shared writable targets.
Assign Prefect read-only access where possible.
Serialize any writes through one agent.
Use per-agent artifact directories.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Marker is a document-processing agent, so its outputs can be treated as facts or extracted text. Prefect is an orchestrator that can route those outputs into downstream tasks or API calls. Without an explicit verification gate, errors from Marker can cascade into Prefect-managed actions, and the profiles do not show a default safeguard that blocks this.
conditions: IF Prefect uses Marker output as task input without validation, THEN extraction errors can propagate downstream.
IF Prefect triggers API calls based on Marker output, THEN incorrect facts can cause incorrect actions.
mitigations: Add validation before Prefect consumes Marker output.
Require human review for high-impact flows.
Use typed schemas for extracted fields.
Log and compare source text against extracted claims.
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds and rejection rules.

E_compliance.rationale: Marker’s profile shows no touched data classes and no network egress, while Prefect touches workflow metadata and has broad egress. The main compliance issue is a policy mismatch if sensitive document content is routed through Prefect-managed metadata or logs. Because the profiles do not show regulated data classes or residency constraints, this is a limited compliance-gap risk rather than a breach by default.
conditions: IF regulated document content is embedded into Prefect workflow metadata or logs, THEN retention and residency policies may diverge.
IF Prefect is configured to retain run history longer than Marker’s source artifacts, THEN deletion/export handling can mismatch.
mitigations: Keep sensitive content out of workflow metadata.
Shorten Prefect log retention.
Document a shared retention policy.
Mask identifiers before orchestration.
requires-engineering: add policy-based redaction for workflow logs.
